exercise.name: Dumbbell Arnold Press

reference.title: Dumbbell Arnold Press
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Shoulders, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder and elbow, with forearm rotation)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in at the start and brace, breathe out as you rotate and press; breathe in on the way down.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s up with the turn, short pause, about 2.5 s down

prescription.tempo: Controlled, about 2-3 s down and 2 s up
prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; usually lighter than for the plain shoulder press (clinical opinion)
prescription.progression: Add reps, then weight; standing Arnold press

cues.text: Sit tall with the back on the pad. Dumbbells in front of the shoulders at chin height, palms facing you, elbows in front and close together.
Breathe out, open the elbows out to the sides and turn the palms forward as you press up.
Finish with arms nearly straight overhead, palms forward.
Reverse it: lower and bring the elbows back in front, turning the palms toward you.
Pause at chin height, palms facing you, and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Rotating first, then pressing (two separate moves)
mistakes.fix: Blend the turn and the press into one smooth arc.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to finish
mistakes.fix: Keep the back on the pad, ribs down; lighten the load.

mistakes.mistake: Dumbbells hitting the face or each other at the start
mistakes.fix: Keep the forearms vertical and the dumbbells a hand width apart in front of the chin.

kinematics.norm: Palms toward the face at the start, palms forward at the top: about a quarter turn of the hands (clinical opinion)
Upper arm in front at about chest height to about 160-170 degrees overhead (clinical opinion)
Elbows travel from in front (flexion plane) out toward the scapular plane as they rise (clinical opinion)
Deeply bent at the start to nearly straight at the top (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #213712, Dumbbell Arnold Press, video (movement reference)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2013, effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses (J Strength Cond Res 27(7):1824-1831)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
No study measured the Arnold press directly; the muscle roles are inferred from shoulder press EMG and anatomy.
modify: Shoulder pain in the opening turn: do the plain seated dumbbell press with palms facing each other.
Stiff shoulders: stop the press short of full overhead.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Works through the whole rep and most at the start, when the elbows are in front (shoulder flexion). Pressing gave the highest anterior deltoid activity among tested exercises (Campos 2020); no EMG study of the Arnold press itself was found.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Works through the whole rep and most at the start, when the elbows are in front (shoulder flexion). Pressing gave the highest anterior deltoid activity among tested exercises (Campos 2020); no EMG study of the Arnold press itself was found.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Takes over as the elbows open out to the sides during the rotation and press (clinical opinion; medial deltoid is high in pressing, Campos 2020).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Takes over as the elbows open out to the sides during the rotation and press (clinical opinion; medial deltoid is high in pressing, Campos 2020).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbow from the deeply bent start to the top.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbow from the deeply bent start to the top.
muscleNotes.pec_r: The clavicular head helps at the start, with the elbows together in front of the chest.
muscleNotes.pec_l: The clavicular head helps at the start, with the elbows together in front of the chest.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upward rotation and elevation of the shoulder blade overhead.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Upward rotation and elevation of the shoulder blade overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade so the arms can finish overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade so the arms can finish overhead.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: controls the turn of the upper arm as the elbows open.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: controls the turn of the upper arm as the elbows open.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Steadies the shoulder as the arms rotate out.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Steadies the shoulder as the arms rotate out.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk against the pad. Core activity is lower seated than standing (Saeterbakken 2012).
